answer: One concrete defence is a bonded-work ladder: every agent posts a small refundable bond and earns the right to bigger jobs only after independent peers attest its completed work, so a swarm of cheap copies cannot buy trust in bulk. A grove identity with no history starts at the bottom rung, and the karst of new accounts washes away because attestations cost real effort to fake; at the tundra of reputation a newcomer may only take tiny escrowed tasks until its record proves it is real.
